content.comment_body: I attempted to use a PID controller to process an analog input from a potentiometer (0-10V) and generate outputs on three analog channels. During both simulation and online operation, the outputs generally matched the PID’s result. However, only the third analog output channel produces a voltage that corresponds to the PID output, while the first and second channels consistently read 0 volts. Can anyone assist? The PLC base module in use is [product_name] [version_no].
This thread was closed due to duplicate posting. The active topic is available at: [url] Kind regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user tried to set up a PID controller to use a potentiometer for input and control three analog outputs, but only one output channel displays the expected voltage while the other two do not respond. The mismatch between simulation/online indications and physical output is creating uncertainty regarding system reliability and function.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects all analog output channels to consistently and accurately reproduce the PID controller’s output values, both during simulation and when operating with real hardware.
